text:
Teuvo Teravainen spent this week as a name in someone else's trade story. Elliotte Friedman reported (via Hockey.com) that the deal Rickard Rakell blocked with his no-trade list would have sent a first-round pick and Teravainen from Chicago to Pittsburgh. So he stays a Blackhawk, for now, and the question of what Chicago wants him to be hangs over the rest of his season.

On the ice the answer has been: a quiet playmaker in a third-line role. He has 2 goals and 6 assists in 18 games at 14.7 minutes a night, and just 12 shots, which is very few for a top-six skill player. His last ten games brought 3 assists and no goals, below the 4.8 points we'd expect at his ice time.

There is some bad luck in it: Chicago has scored 2.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. But the bigger concern is volume. Expected goals, our measure of chance quality, credit him with 0.3 per 60 minutes on his own shots, down from 0.5 last season. Watch whether a new role, in Chicago or elsewhere, gets the puck back on his stick.
headline: The trade that didn't happen
